# az-tf-mlz-user-assigned-identity

A Fortytwo managed landing zone (MLZ) module for one user-assigned managed identity
(`Microsoft.ManagedIdentity/userAssignedIdentities`) and its federated identity credentials, in AzAPI:
the Azure Monitor Agent's identity, identities for customer-managed keys and Key Vault access, and
deployment identities that pipelines sign in as through OpenID Connect (GitHub Actions and others).

- **Federated identity credentials** (`federated_identity_credentials`, keyed by credential name; up to
  20 per identity) trust tokens from an external identity provider by `issuer`, `subject` and one
  audience (`api://AzureADTokenExchange` by default). Azure refuses parallel credential writes under one
  identity, so they are written one at a time (`modules/federated_identity_credential`, which can also be
  called alone with an identity's resource ID). A changed issuer, subject or audience is written in
  place; a renamed credential is replaced. A new credential can take a few minutes to work: until it has
  replicated, sign-ins fail with `AADSTS70021`.
- **The identity's lock and role assignments** through
  [`az-tf-mlz-interfaces`](https://github.com/fortytwoservices/az-tf-mlz-interfaces). The lock also
  covers the credentials, so it is removed around any change to them. `role_assignments` are roles **on
  the identity** (for example Managed Identity Operator for whoever assigns it to resources); roles
  **for** the identity belong to the target resource's module (its `role_assignments`) or to
  [`az-tf-mlz-role-assignment`](https://github.com/fortytwoservices/az-tf-mlz-role-assignment), with
  `principal_id` set to this module's `principal_id` and `principal_type = "ServicePrincipal"`.
- **`isolation_scope`** `None` (Azure's default) or `Regional`, which lets only resources in the
  identity's region use it. No diagnostic settings: identities have none.

```hcl
module "deployment_identity" {
  source = "git::https://github.com/fortytwoservices/az-tf-mlz-user-assigned-identity.git?ref=vX.Y.Z"

  name      = "id-platform-deploy"
  parent_id = azapi_resource.resource_group.id
  location  = "swedencentral"
  federated_identity_credentials = {
    github-production = {
      issuer  = "https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com"
      subject = "repo:<owner>/<repo>:environment:production"
    }
  }
  lock = { kind = "CanNotDelete" }
}
```

Things to know:

- A `ReadOnly` lock blocks updates of the identity itself (tags, isolation scope): remove it first.
  Credentials can be added, changed and removed under either lock kind.
- The pair of `issuer` and `subject` must be unique per identity, and no property takes wildcards.
  Matching subjects by expression (flexible federated identity credentials) is a preview that only
  preview API versions accept, so this module does not offer it yet.
- GitHub's subjects carry the repository's owner and name (`repo:<owner>/<repo>:...`), or, in the
  immutable format that repositories created, renamed or transferred after 2026-07-15 use, also their
  IDs (`repo:<owner>@<owner-id>/<repo>@<repo-id>:...`). Copy the prefix from the repository's OIDC
  settings: a subject that does not match fails the sign-in without saying why.
- Azure does not support federated identity credentials on identities in Malaysia South.

Examples: `default` (an identity with a role assignment on it) and `github_actions` (a deployment
identity with credentials for a repository's environment and its pull requests).

## Optional Inputs

The following input variables are optional (have default values):

### <a name="input_federated_identity_credentials"></a> [federated\_identity\_credentials](#input\_federated\_identity\_credentials)

Description: Federated identity credentials on the user-assigned identity, keyed by credential name (3 to 120 characters:  
letters, digits, hyphens and underscores, starting with a letter or digit; renaming one replaces it). Azure  
allows 20 per identity, each with its own pair of `issuer` and `subject`. No property takes wildcards.

- `issuer` - URL of the external identity provider, for example `https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com` (up to 600 characters).
- `subject` - Identifier of the external workload, for example `repo:<owner>/<repo>:environment:<name>`; it must match the token's `sub` claim exactly (up to 600 characters).
- `audiences` - (Optional) The audience accepted in the external token; Azure takes exactly one (up to 600 characters). Defaults to `["api://AzureADTokenExchange"]`.

Type:

```hcl
map(object({
    issuer    = string
    subject   = string
    audiences = optional(list(string), ["api://AzureADTokenExchange"])
  }))
```

Default: `{}`

### <a name="input_ignore_body_changes"></a> [ignore\_body\_changes](#input\_ignore\_body\_changes)

Description: Paths in each resource's `body` whose changes the AzAPI provider ignores. Prefer Terraform's `lifecycle.ignore_changes` when the paths are static; use this variable when the paths must be derived from variables or other non-static values.

Paths use dot notation, for example `properties.isolationScope`. Individual list items cannot be targeted; ignore the whole list property instead. Configuration changes at an ignored path are **not** sent to Azure until that path is removed from the list. Changes take effect only after an apply, because the value is held in provider-private state.

- `managedidentity_user_assigned_identities` - Ignored body paths for the user-assigned identity.
- `authorization_locks` - Ignored body paths for the lock.
- `authorization_role_assignments` - Ignored body paths for the role assignments.
- `managedidentity_user_assigned_identities_federated_identity_credentials` - Slot for the `federated_identity_credential` submodule.
  - `managedidentity_user_assigned_identities_federated_identity_credentials` - Ignored body paths for each federated identity credential.

Type:

```hcl
object({
    managedidentity_user_assigned_identities = optional(list(string), [])
    authorization_locks                      = optional(list(string), [])
    authorization_role_assignments           = optional(list(string), [])

    managedidentity_user_assigned_identities_federated_identity_credentials = optional(object({
      managedidentity_user_assigned_identities_federated_identity_credentials = optional(list(string), [])
    }), {})
  })
```

Default: `{}`

### <a name="input_isolation_scope"></a> [isolation\_scope](#input\_isolation\_scope)

Description: Regional restriction on assigning the identity: `None` (Azure's default) or `Regional`.

Type: `string`

Default: `"None"`

### <a name="input_lock"></a> [lock](#input\_lock)

Description: Controls the Resource Lock configuration for this resource. The following properties can be specified:

- `kind` - (Required) The type of lock. Possible values are `\"CanNotDelete\"` and `\"ReadOnly\"`.
- `name` - (Optional) The name of the lock. If not specified, a name will be generated based on the `kind` value. Changing this forces the creation of a new resource.
- `notes` - (Optional) Notes about the lock. This value maps to `Microsoft.Authorization/locks.properties.notes`.

Type:

```hcl
object({
    kind  = string
    name  = optional(string, null)
    notes = optional(string, null)
  })
```

Default: `null`

### <a name="input_resource_types"></a> [resource\_types](#input\_resource\_types)

Description: Override the AzAPI `<provider>/<resource>@<api-version>` strings used by this module and its submodule. Each key defaults to a tested value; supply only the keys you want to override.

- `managedidentity_user_assigned_identities` - The user-assigned identity.
- `authorization_locks` - The lock on the user-assigned identity.
- `authorization_role_assignments` - Role assignments on the user-assigned identity.
- `managedidentity_user_assigned_identities_federated_identity_credentials` - Slot for the `federated_identity_credential` submodule. Defaults live in the submodule.
  - `managedidentity_user_assigned_identities_federated_identity_credentials` - Each federated identity credential.

Type:

```hcl
object({
    managedidentity_user_assigned_identities = optional(string, "Microsoft.ManagedIdentity/userAssignedIdentities@2024-11-30")
    authorization_locks                      = optional(string, "Microsoft.Authorization/locks@2020-05-01")
    authorization_role_assignments           = optional(string, "Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments@2022-04-01")

    managedidentity_user_assigned_identities_federated_identity_credentials = optional(object({
      managedidentity_user_assigned_identities_federated_identity_credentials = optional(string)
    }), {})
  })
```

Default: `{}`

### <a name="input_role_assignments"></a> [role\_assignments](#input\_role\_assignments)

Description: A map of role assignments to create on the user-assigned identity. The map key is deliberately arbitrary to avoid issues where map keys maybe unknown at plan time.

- `name` - (Optional) The name of the role assignment. If not set, a random UUID will be generated. Changing this forces the creation of a new resource.
- `role_definition_id_or_name` - The ID or name of the role definition to assign to the principal.
- `principal_id` - The ID of the principal to assign the role to.
- `description` - (Optional) The description of the role assignment.
- `skip_service_principal_aad_check` - (Optional) If set to true, skips the Azure Active Directory check for the service principal in the tenant. Defaults to false.
- `condition` - (Optional) The condition which will be used to scope the role assignment.
- `condition_version` - (Optional) The version of the condition syntax. Leave as `null` if you are not using a condition, if you are then valid values are '2.0'.
- `delegated_managed_identity_resource_id` - (Optional) The delegated Azure Resource Id which contains a Managed Identity. Changing this forces a new resource to be created. This field is only used in cross-tenant scenario.
- `principal_type` - (Optional) The type of the `principal_id`. Possible values are `User`, `Group` and `ServicePrincipal`. It is necessary to explicitly set this attribute when creating role assignments if the principal creating the assignment is constrained by ABAC rules that filters on the PrincipalType attribute.

> Note: only set `skip_service_principal_aad_check` to true if you are assigning a role to a service principal.

Type:

```hcl
map(object({
    name                                   = optional(string, null)
    role_definition_id_or_name             = string
    principal_id                           = string
    description                            = optional(string, null)
    skip_service_principal_aad_check       = optional(bool, false)
    condition                              = optional(string, null)
    condition_version                      = optional(string, null)
    delegated_managed_identity_resource_id = optional(string, null)
    principal_type                         = optional(string, null)
  }))
```

Default: `{}`

## Development

Tools: Terraform 1.17.0, TFLint 0.65.0, terraform-docs 0.24.0 (the versions CI uses).

| What | Command |
|---|---|
| Format, validate, lint, unit tests, README drift (what CI runs) | `scripts/check.sh` |
| Format the code and regenerate the READMEs first | `scripts/check.sh --fix` |
| Integration tests in Azure | `ARM_SUBSCRIPTION_ID=<test subscription> scripts/integration.sh [dir ...]` |
| Examples: apply, plan again (must be empty), destroy | `ARM_SUBSCRIPTION_ID=<test subscription> scripts/e2e.sh [examples/<name> ...]` |

`README.md` files are generated from `_header.md`, the code and `_footer.md`; do not edit them by hand.

## Versions and releases

Every release is a SemVer tag `vX.Y.Z`; tags never move, and `main` is never consumed. Pin a release:

```hcl
source = "git::https://github.com/fortytwoservices/<repository>.git?ref=vX.Y.Z"
```

Pull requests are squash-merged, and their titles follow Conventional Commits, which set the next
version: `fix:` a patch, `feat:` a minor (a patch before 1.0.0), `feat!:` or `fix!:` a major (a minor
before 1.0.0). `docs:`, `test:`, `ci:`, `chore:` and `refactor:` release nothing. release-please keeps a
release pull request open; merging it writes `CHANGELOG.md`, the tag and the GitHub release.
